newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares inch down, seen staying flat.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares inch down, seen staying flat.

text.p: Polish shares eased 0.2 percent after a five-session gain that followed steep falls, and analysts said the market would likely stay flat on Friday.

"I don't see any signal which would mobilise demand," said Dariusz Szepieniec of Bank Slaski brokerage, adding though that the market might still have some upward potential in the near term after last week's 6.1-percent fall.
Analysts said negative signals existed, such as a heavy primary market offer beginning next week with paper firm Celuloza Swiecie's public offering of at least 112.5 million zlotys.
Analysts also said the threat of falls on foreign bourses from concerns about interest rate rises could continue to slow buying in Warsaw as well.
The main market's all-share WIG index inched down 0.2 percent to 16,333.1 points and turnover eased 4.4 percent to 186.3 million zlotys on all three markets.

Analysts said Kable jumped 8.6 percent to 49 zlotys in heavy trade, extending Wednesday's surge after 50-percent owner NKT Cables called a public tender offer to buy Kable's remaining one million shares.
NKT Cables offered to buy the remaining shares at Kable's then market price of 41 zlotys. Analysts said the firm's shares should now lose steam or fall.

Some analysts were surprised by the scale of biggest loser Swarzedz's 8.9-percent tumble. The furniture maker had fallen 3.1 percent on Wednesday after surging both before and after Monday's debt restructuring deal with creditors.
